tagline: Trat's island arc — car-ferry dependency and an emerging island-hopping network.
summary: Koh Chang is Thailand's second-largest island, set in Trat province near the Cambodian border and ringed by the Mu Ko Chang marine national park. Access today runs through car ferries from Laem Ngop, while onward island-hopping to Koh Mak, Koh Kood and Koh Wai launches from Bang Bao on wooden boats and speedboats. It is a frontier market with real pull — Trat's tourism has been surging, and Koh Chang itself carries a growing premium-eco reputation — but the longer mainland crossings range-gate the network to intra-archipelago Pioneer II hops, with the Bangkok link a longer-range play. The quiet, low-wake foiling story lands especially well inside a marine national park where diesel boats jar against the conservation brand.

use_cases.title: Bang Bao island-hopping (Mak / Kood / Wai)
use_cases.body: A smooth, near-silent foiling service across the tight Koh Chang archipelago, linking Bang Bao to Koh Mak, Koh Kood and Koh Wai. It replaces slow wooden boats and bumpy speedboats with a calm ride that lets guests breakfast on one island and lunch on another.

use_cases.title: Low-wake national-park transfers
use_cases.body: Inside the Mu Ko Chang marine national park, a zero-wake electric foiling craft moves guests without the noise, fumes and reef-stressing wash of diesel boats. The eco-positioning is one a diesel fleet simply cannot match in a protected-water setting.

use_cases.title: Resort-guest premium shuttle
use_cases.body: On-demand foiling transfers between Koh Chang's resorts and the surrounding islands give high-value guests a signature, smooth arrival. It turns the inter-island leg from a logistics chore into part of the stay.

journeys.today: Wooden boat or speedboat, ~30-60 min, fully weather-exposed and seasonally curtailed.
journeys.with_navier: A quick, calm foiling crossing that flies above the chop and holds its schedule.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The intra-archipelago legs all sit well inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope — Ao Sapparot↔Bang Bao (~8 nm) and Bang Bao↔Koh Mak (~11 nm) — and the zero-wake, near-silent ride is the ideal fit for the protected waters of the Mu Ko Chang marine national park.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta LR's ~2,000 nm hybrid range, with no charging-infrastructure dependency, is what could carry the longer mainland and Bangkok-direction links that all-electric range and sparse island grid power cannot yet support — sequencing the frontier corridors without waiting on shore charging.

competitive_landscape: Car ferries (Centrepoint, Ferry Koh Chang) from Laem Ngop; wooden island-hopping boats from Bang Bao — no premium electric option.
seasonality: Peak: Nov-Apr. Strong SW monsoon May-Oct closes many island-hopping routes; tight seasonal gating.
regulatory_note: Thai cabotage + Marine Department licensing; proximity to Cambodia border adds maritime-zone caution for routing.
